title: Respiration and Circulation
subject: Biology
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET / NEET • Quick Revision

nodes.title: Human Respiratory System & Mechanism of Breathing
points: Respiratory tract: External nares → Nasal cavity (vestibule, respiratory, olfactory) → Pharynx → Larynx (voice box with thyroid cartilage, epiglottis) → Trachea (C-shaped hyaline cartilage rings) → Primary bronchi → Bronchioles → Alveoli (~300 million in lungs; surface area ~70-100 m²; Type I cells for gas exchange, Type II cells secrete dipalmitoyl phosphatidylcholine surfactant to prevent collapse).

Inspiration (Active, 2 sec): Contraction of Diaphragm (flattens) + Contraction of External Intercostal Muscles (EICM pulls ribs upward and outward) → Increases thoracic volume → Intrapulmonary pressure drops below atmospheric (−2 to −3 mmHg) → Air rushes in.
Expiration (Passive, 3 sec): Relaxation of diaphragm and EICM → Thoracic volume decreases → Intrapulmonary pressure rises above atmospheric (+2 to +3 mmHg) → Air expelled.

formulas.label: Breathing pressure-volume relation (Boyle's Law)
formulas.expr: Thoracic volume increases → Intrapulmonary pressure drops below P_atm → Air inflow (Inspiration)

formulas.label: Pulmonary surfactant composition
formulas.expr: Dipalmitoyl lecithin / Phosphatidylcholine (secreted by Type II pneumocytes to lower surface tension)

nodes.title: Respiratory Volumes and Capacities
points: Tidal Volume (TV): Volume inspired/expired in normal breath = 500 mL (~6000-8000 mL/min).
Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV): Extra volume inspired forcefully = 2500 - 3000 mL.
Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV): Extra volume expired forcefully = 1000 - 1100 mL.
Residual Volume (RV): Volume remaining in lungs after maximal expiration = 1100 - 1200 mL (cannot be measured by spirometer!).
Inspiratory Capacity (IC) = TV + IRV = 3000 - 3500 mL.
Functional Residual Capacity (FRC) = ERV + RV = 2100 - 2300 mL.
Vital Capacity (VC) = ERV + TV + IRV = 3500 - 4500 mL (maximum air expired after maximal inspiration).
Total Lung Capacity (TLC) = VC + RV = 5000 - 6000 mL. Dead space volume = 150 mL.

formulas.label: Vital Capacity (VC) formula
formulas.expr: VC = TV + IRV + ERV (approx 4000 - 4600 mL)

formulas.label: Total Lung Capacity (TLC) formula
formulas.expr: TLC = VC + RV = TV + IRV + ERV + RV (approx 5500 - 6000 mL)

formulas.label: Functional Residual Capacity (FRC)
formulas.expr: FRC = ERV + RV (air remaining after normal expiration, ~2200 mL)

nodes.title: Gas Exchange & Transport of Oxygen and Carbon Dioxide
points: Partial pressures: Alveolar air (pO₂ = 104 mmHg, pCO₂ = 40 mmHg); Deoxygenated blood (pO₂ = 40, pCO₂ = 45); Oxygenated blood (pO₂ = 95, pCO₂ = 40); Tissues (pO₂ = 40, pCO₂ = 45).
Oxygen transport: 3% dissolved in plasma; 97% as Oxyhemoglobin (Hb₄O₈). 1 g Hb binds 1.34 mL O₂. 100 mL blood carries ~20 mL O₂, delivering ~5 mL O₂ to resting tissues.

Oxygen-Hemoglobin Dissociation Curve: Sigmoid shaped. Bohr Effect: Shift of curve to the RIGHT (lowered Hb-O₂ affinity, releasing O₂ to tissues) caused by: ↑ pCO₂, ↑ [H⁺] / ↓ pH, ↑ Temperature, ↑ 2,3-BPG.
Carbon dioxide transport: 7% dissolved in plasma; 23% as Carbaminohaemoglobin (Hb·CO₂); 70% as Bicarbonate ions (HCO₃⁻).

Chloride Shift (Hamburger Phenomenon): Fast carbonic anhydrase in RBC converts CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃ ⇌ H⁺ + HCO₃⁻. HCO₃⁻ diffuses into plasma; Cl⁻ moves from plasma INTO RBC to maintain electrical neutrality.

formulas.label: Carbonic anhydrase reaction
formulas.expr: CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃ ⇌ H⁺ + HCO₃⁻ (fastest enzyme, zinc-dependent)

formulas.label: Bohr effect (Right shift factors)
formulas.expr: Right shift = Lowers Hb-O₂ affinity (↑ pCO₂, ↑ H⁺ / ↓ pH, ↑ Temp, ↑ 2,3-DPG)

formulas.label: Chloride shift (Hamburger phenomenon)
formulas.expr: HCO₃⁻ leaves RBC to plasma ↔ Cl⁻ enters RBC from plasma (maintains ionic balance)

nodes.title: Blood Composition & Coagulation Cascade
points: Blood: Fluid connective tissue (pH 7.4). Plasma (55%) + Formed elements (45%).

Formed elements: 1) RBCs (Erythrocytes, 5-5.5 million/mm³, biconcave, enucleated, lifespan 120 days, destroyed in spleen); 2) WBCs (Leukocytes, 5000-10000/mm³; Neutrophils 60-65% phagocytic, Eosinophils 2-3% allergic, Basophils 0.5-1% histamine/heparin, Lymphocytes 20-25% B & T cells, Monocytes 6-8% macrophages); 3) Platelets (Thrombocytes, 1.5-3.5 lakh/mm³, megakaryocyte fragments).

Blood Clotting Cascade (3 Stages): 1) Thromboplastin released by damaged tissues/platelets forms Prothrombinase (Thrombokinase) in presence of Ca²⁺; 2) Prothrombinase converts inactive Prothrombin into active Thrombin; 3) Thrombin converts soluble Fibrinogen into insoluble Fibrin mesh trapping blood cells to form clot.

formulas.label: Blood clotting 3-step cascade
formulas.expr: Thromboplastin + Ca²⁺ → Prothrombinase; Prothrombin → Thrombin; Fibrinogen → Fibrin clot

formulas.label: Normal blood counts benchmark
formulas.expr: RBC: 5.0 - 5.5 million/µL | WBC: 5000 - 10000/µL | Platelets: 1.5 - 3.5 lakh/µL | pH = 7.4

nodes.title: Blood Groups & Rh Incompatibility (Erythroblastosis Fetalis)
points: ABO System (Karl Landsteiner): A (Antigen A, Antibody anti-B); B (Antigen B, Antibody anti-A); AB (Antigens A and B, NO antibodies; Universal Recipient); O (NO antigens, Antibodies anti-A and anti-B; Universal Donor).
Rh System (Landsteiner & Wiener): Rh⁺ (contains Rh antigen D, ~85% humans) vs Rh⁻.

Erythroblastosis Fetalis (HDN): Occurs when Rh⁻ mother carries Rh⁺ fetus. During 1st delivery, fetal Rh⁺ RBCs leak into maternal circulation, inducing anti-Rh antibody production. In subsequent Rh⁺ pregnancy, maternal anti-Rh IgG antibodies cross placenta, hemolyzing fetal RBCs (causes severe anemia, jaundice, kernicterus, fetal death).
Prevention: Administering anti-D antibodies (Rhogam injection) to Rh⁻ mother within 72 hours of delivering first Rh⁺ baby.

formulas.label: Erythroblastosis fetalis parentage setup
formulas.expr: Mother: Rh⁻ | Father: Rh⁺ | Fetus: Rh⁺ (risk in 2nd and subsequent Rh⁺ pregnancies)

formulas.label: Prevention with Rhogam
formulas.expr: Administer anti-D antibodies (Rhogam) to Rh⁻ mother within 72 hours of 1st delivery

formulas.label: ABO blood groups compatibility
formulas.expr: Universal Donor: O⁻ (no ABO or Rh antigens) | Universal Recipient: AB⁺ (no plasma antibodies)

nodes.title: Human Heart Anatomy & Conducting System
points: Heart anatomy: Mesodermal, myogenic, 4 chambers (2 atria, 2 ventricles). Enclosed in double-walled pericardium with pericardial fluid. Left ventricular wall is 3 times thicker than right.

Valves: Tricuspid valve (between right atrium and right ventricle, 3 cusps held by chordae tendineae to papillary muscles); Bicuspid / Mitral valve (between left atrium and left ventricle, 2 cusps); Semilunar valves (pulmonary and aortic).

Conducting System: 1) SA Node (Pacemaker): Upper right atrium near SVC opening; fires rhythmic impulses at ~72/min; 2) AV Node (Pace-setter): Lower left interatrial septum; introduces 0.1 sec delay; 3) Bundle of His: Interventricular septum; 4) Purkinje Fibers: Ventricular walls conducting impulse rapidly (~4 m/s) to trigger ventricular contraction from apex upward.

formulas.label: Cardiac impulse conduction pathway
formulas.expr: SA Node (Pacemaker, 72/min) → AV Node (Pace-setter) → Bundle of His → Purkinje Fibers → Ventricular Myocardium

formulas.label: Atrioventricular valves matching
formulas.expr: Right side = Tricuspid valve (3 flaps) | Left side = Bicuspid / Mitral valve (2 flaps)

nodes.title: Cardiac Cycle, Cardiac Output & Heart Sounds
points: Cardiac Cycle: Complete heartbeat cycle lasting 0.8 seconds (at 72 bpm):
1. Joint Diastole (0.4 sec): All chambers relax; semilunar valves closed; AV valves open; ventricles fill to 70% passively.
2. Atrial Systole (0.1 sec): SA node fires; atria contract, pumping remaining 30% blood into ventricles.
3. Ventricular Systole (0.3 sec): Ventricles contract; AV valves snap shut producing 1st heart sound 'LUBB'; semilunar valves open, ejecting blood into aorta/pulmonary artery.
4. Ventricular Diastole (0.5 sec): Ventricles relax; semilunar valves snap shut producing 2nd heart sound 'DUPP'.
Stroke Volume (SV) = 70 mL/beat. Cardiac Output (CO) = SV × HR = 70 mL × 72 bpm ≈ 5040 mL/min (~5 L/min).

formulas.label: Cardiac Cycle duration breakdown (0.8 sec)
formulas.expr: Atrial Systole (0.1 s) + Atrial Diastole (0.7 s) = 0.8 s | Ventricular Systole (0.3 s) + Ventricular Diastole (0.5 s) = 0.8 s

formulas.label: Cardiac Output fundamental formula
formulas.expr: CO = SV × HR (e.g. 70 mL/beat × 72 beats/min = 5040 mL/min ≈ 5.0 L/min)

formulas.label: Heart sounds key differences
formulas.expr: LUBB = AV valves closure (longer, low pitch) | DUPP = Semilunar valves closure (shorter, high pitch)

nodes.title: Blood Pressure, Electrocardiogram (ECG) & Disorders
points: Blood Pressure (BP): Measured using Sphygmomanometer over brachial artery. Normal BP = 120 / 80 mmHg (Systolic / Diastolic). Pulse Pressure = Systolic − Diastolic = 40 mmHg. Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP) = Diastolic + (Pulse Pressure / 3) ≈ 93.3 mmHg.
Electrocardiogram (ECG): Graphical record of electrical activity of heart (Einthoven): P wave (Atrial depolarization); QRS complex (Ventricular depolarization); T wave (Ventricular repolarization).

Cardiovascular Disorders: 1) Hypertension: Sustained BP > 140/90 mmHg; 2) Atherosclerosis / CAD: Deposition of calcium, fat, and cholesterol narrowing arterial lumen; 3) Angina Pectoris: Acute chest pain due to myocardial ischemia; 4) Myocardial Infarction: Heart attack due to coronary artery occlusion.

formulas.label: Normal Blood Pressure coordinates
formulas.expr: Systolic BP = 120 mmHg | Diastolic BP = 80 mmHg | Pulse Pressure = 120 − 80 = 40 mmHg

formulas.label: Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP) formula
formulas.expr: MAP = Diastolic BP + (Pulse Pressure / 3) = 80 + (40 / 3) ≈ 93.3 mmHg

formulas.label: ECG waves interpretation key
formulas.expr: P wave = Atrial depolarization | QRS complex = Ventricular depolarization | T wave = Ventricular repolarization

nodes.title: High-Weightage Board Questions & Diagrams
points: Board Diagram 1: Internal structure of Human Heart (label: atria, ventricles, bicuspid, tricuspid, semilunar valves, chordae tendineae, fossa ovalis).
Board Diagram 2: Conducting system of human heart (SA node, AV node, Bundle of His, Purkinje fibers).
Board Diagram 3: Standard ECG wave and label P, QRS, T waves.
Board Distinguish 1: Artery vs Vein (thick muscular tunica media, narrow lumen, no valves vs thin wall, wide lumen, semilunar valves).
Board Distinguish 2: First heart sound (Lubb) vs Second heart sound (Dupp).

formulas.label: Artery vs Vein anatomical distinction
formulas.expr: Artery: Thick tunica media, narrow lumen, high pressure, no valves | Vein: Thin media, wide lumen, semilunar valves

formulas.label: Oxygen dissociation curve coordinates
formulas.expr: P₅₀ value (pO₂ at 50% Hb saturation) ≈ 26 to 27 mmHg

nodes.title: MHT-CET & NEET High-Speed Shortcuts & Traps
points: TRAP 1: Pacemaker of heart: SA node (fires 70-75 impulses/min). AV node is pace-setter (40-60 impulses/min). If SA node fails, AV node takes over.
TRAP 2: Cardiac output calculation: CO = Stroke Volume × Heart Rate. Athletes have higher stroke volume, hence lower resting heart rate (bradycardia) to maintain identical cardiac output!
TRAP 3: Residual Volume (RV) CANNOT be measured by standard spirometer! Consequently, FRC (ERV + RV) and TLC (VC + RV) cannot be measured by spirometry alone.
TRAP 4: Carbonic anhydrase is the fastest enzyme known (~600,000 molecules/sec) and requires Zinc (Zn²⁺) as essential cofactor.
TRAP 5: Universal donor vs Universal recipient: O⁻ (negative) is TRUE universal donor because it lacks A, B, and Rh antigens. AB⁺ (positive) is TRUE universal recipient.

formulas.label: Cardiac Output stroke volume relation
formulas.expr: CO = SV × HR (e.g. at HR 75 bpm & SV 70 mL → CO = 5.25 L/min)

formulas.label: Non-measurable spirometric volumes
formulas.expr: RV, FRC, and TLC CANNOT be directly measured by spirometry

formulas.label: True universal blood donor/recipient
formulas.expr: Universal Donor = O Rh⁻ (O negative) | Universal Recipient = AB Rh⁺ (AB positive)
